page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 96 vCPUs and 360 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The CPU allocation is fully dedicated, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of a 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom-quartile scores in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. However, the massive core count enables strong multi-core performance, placing it in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 3918.64 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 213.36 GB/sec, both ranking in the top tier. Conversely, single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing perform poorly, while multi-threaded decompression and database operations achieve average, stable throughput.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports key instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA, which aids in extended instruction tests. However, it lacks modern accelerators such as AVX-512 VNNI, AVX VNNI, and AMX, resulting in poor performance for tasks like LLM text generation. Given these characteristics, the n1-standard-96 is best suited for highly parallelized, general-purpose workloads that can leverage its high core count and strong memory bandwidth, such as multi-threaded data processing, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations, rather than single-threaded applications or modern AI inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose instance configured with 96 vCPUs and 360 GB of RAM on a dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture. Featuring 48 physical cores with hyper-threading, it lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data highlights a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance: single-threaded operations and text processing rank in the bottom 25%, whereas multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth (reaching 3918.64 GB/sec for cached reads) rank in the top 25%. While the hardware supports AVX-512F and AES, the absence of newer instruction sets like AMX or AVX-512 VNNI limits its efficiency in modern AI text generation. Consequently, this instance is highly suited for parallelized general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dense core counts rather than raw single-core speed.
